identity.title: Evaluating Robustness of Reasoning Models on Parameterized Logical Problems

problem.claim: Evaluate LLM-based reasoners on structured logical problems and their robustness to semantics-preserving changes.

gap.claim: Standard SAT-style benchmarks may conflate surface difficulty with structural factors determining satisfiability, obscuring distinct brittleness regimes.

contributions.claim: Introduces a diagnostic 2-SAT benchmark based on parameterized structured 2-CNF families with interpretable control axes.
Provides generators targeting contradiction cores, solution multiplicity, propagation, late clause coupling, and symmetry or redundancy handling.
Evaluates decision accuracy, assignment validity, and robustness to clause reordering, filler clauses, and variable renaming.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed benchmark distinguishes structural reasoning phenomena through parameterized 2-SAT families and targeted interventions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report sharp performance transitions under targeted structural interventions, including when surface statistics are held fixed.
The authors report that these interventions reveal brittleness regimes not visible in aggregate SAT accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Logic is presented as a controlled testbed, while standard SAT benchmarks may confound surface and structural difficulty.
A parameterized structured 2-SAT benchmark is introduced, with satisfiability characterized through implication graphs.
Generators vary contradiction cores, free variables, planted backbones, late bridges, and symmetry or duplication.
Reasoners are assessed on decisions, assignments, and robustness to semantics-preserving perturbations.
Targeted structural changes produce sharp performance transitions and expose hidden brittleness.

source_observation.claim: The abstract varies specific structural properties while holding surface statistics fixed and reports transitions that aggregate accuracy misses.

lessons.interpretation: Parameterizing one interpretable factor at a time can make failure boundaries more diagnostically legible.
lessons.application: Construct evaluation families that sweep a structural variable while matching length, wording, and clause-order statistics.
lessons.exception: This is unsuitable when the target task lacks a meaningful structural parameter or matched perturbations cannot preserve semantics.

unknowns: The abstract does not report model identities, dataset sizes, numerical accuracies, transition thresholds, or statistical uncertainty.
It does not specify how assignment validity is checked or which structural axes drive particular model failures.
